components.description: Flat form. Use either this or the components nested inside courses.

steps.description: Flat form. Use either this or the steps nested inside components.

Menu.title: Menu
Menu.description: A multi-course dinner broken into atomic steps and the dependencies between them. Write it nested or flat. All content text (names, titles, details, ingredients) is in Finnish; field names and station values are not.

order.description: Optional; defaults to the course position in the array.

components.description: Nested form. Omit when the components live at the root of the menu.

courseId.description: Flat form only; the nested form takes it from the enclosing course.

steps.description: Nested form. Omit when the steps live at the root of the menu instead.

Component.title: Osa (component)
Component.description: One part of a course — in practice one dish or side.

id.description: Optional; derived from the title when omitted.

componentId.description: Flat form only; the nested form takes it from the enclosing component.

title.description: A short imperative, in Finnish. E.g. "Kuori ja pilko sipuli".

detail.description: The full instruction, in Finnish. Cooking times belong here — steps have no duration field.

station.description: Where the work physically happens. Only name equipment several dishes might compete for; bench work, cold prep and plating are all "muu". liesi = stovetop, uuni = oven, grilli = grill, muu = anything else.

deps.description: Steps that must be finished before this one may start. Either a step id or a step title verbatim; titles are resolved to ids on import, and a title matching two steps is an error rather than a guess.

uses.description: Ingredients this step consumes, spelled exactly as in the component's ingredients list.

holdPoint.description: True when the step can be finished well ahead of service. Everything downstream of a hold point is last-minute work.

Step.title: Vaihe (step)
Step.description: One atomic piece of work: what one cook must finish in one go.
